name: Datum Pipe
tagline: Pipe stress analysis on the desktop: displacements, support loads, nozzle loads and code stresses, with an automatic isometric.
for: Piping, stress, mechanical, process and plant engineers, consultants and students.
about: Datum Pipe works out how a piping system moves and what it pushes on when it heats up, carries its weight and holds its pressure. You type the piping as a table of elements, the way a stress engineer marks up an isometric, and it appears in 3D as you type: pipes at their true diameter, bends, tees, reducers, valves, flanges and supports.

Put on the supports, temperatures, pressures and equipment movements; the load cases are built for you. Analyze solves every case with Datum Pipe's own 3D pipe element solver, checks the stresses using the equations of the process piping code (ASME B31.3), and shows the results on the model, in tables of displacements, support loads and nozzle loads, on an automatic isometric drawing and in a printed stress report. Allowable stresses are your inputs, and Help › Verification solves benchmark problems with known answers in front of you.

steps.title: Route the piping
steps.text: Type each element's From node, To node and lengths in the table; pick the pipe, material, line conditions and component (bend, tee, reducer, valve, flange). It draws in 3D at once.

steps.title: Support and load it
steps.text: Add anchors, rests, guides, line stops, springs and nozzle points; set up to three operating temperatures and pressures, the hydrotest and equipment movements.

steps.title: Check and report
steps.text: Analyze, see the stress ratios on the model, read the support and nozzle loads, and print the stress report with the isometric and the equilibrium checks.

highlights: An element table that draws the piping in 3D as you type: true diameters, insulation, bends, tees, reducers, valves, flanges and support symbols
Pipe sizes ½" to 24" in every schedule, five piping materials with properties against temperature and their sources, and your own sizes and materials
Anchors, one-way rests, guides, line stops and restraints with gaps and friction, skewed restraints, springs, constant-force supports and imposed equipment movements
Load cases built for you: sustained, operating, expansion range, hydrotest, and wind and static seismic as occasional cases

Code stresses calculated using the equations of the process piping code: hoop stress and minimum wall (straight pipe, bends at their intrados, both ends of reducers), sustained stress, the displacement stress range and occasional stress, with PASS or FAIL at every point
Support loads for the civil team and nozzle loads in the nozzle's own axes, checked against your allowables
An automatic isometric drawing with dimensions, node numbers and result tags, and a printed stress report
Help › Verification: benchmark problems with known answers solved in front of you, and an equilibrium check after every solve; Help › Sources: where every equation is published
